newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam, China hold post-Deng meeting.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam, China hold post-Deng meeting.

text.p: Vietnam's Communist Party reported on Monday a rare meeting between a member of its executive politburo and Chinese President Jiang Zemin, one day after Beijing announced the death of paramount leader Deng Xiaoping.

An official with the party central committee's external affairs office told Reuters that Jiang and Nguyen Tan Dung had discussed relations between the two countries' ruling communist parties during a meeting on Friday.

No details were available but the official confirmed press reports that Dung had stressed the need to "continue preserving, treasuring and boosting" existing agreements between the leadership in both countries.
Dung, whose visit was previously unpublicised, arrived in China last Tuesday for a 10-day visit -- two days before Deng's death was announced in Beijing.
Vietnam reacted coolly to news of his death. Deng is viewed by Hanoi as the man responsible for hostile policy towards Vietnam during the late 1970s and 80s.
A formal message of condolence last week pointedly referred to his demise as a loss for China, but avoided the traditional accolades of friendship applied to a socialist leader of Deng's stature.
State newspapers said Jiang, who is also general secretary of China's Communist Party, had thanked Dung for the condolences and said he hoped that regular contacts would continue.
Dung, whose responsibilities include economic policy, was appointed to Vietnam's highest political body at a party congress last year. He is also a member of the inner politburo's standing committee.
